title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 192 (Restriction on non-cash transactions involving directors)

content.overview: Section 192 provides that a company shall not enter into an arrangement by which a director of the company or its holding, subsidiary or associate company, or a person connected with him, acquires or is to acquire assets for consideration other than cash from the company, or the company acquires or is to acquire assets for consideration other than cash from such a director or connected person, unless the arrangement is previously approved by a resolution of the company in general meeting. If the director or connected person is a director of its holding company, approval of the holding company in general meeting is also required. Notice of the resolution must include the particulars of the arrangement and the value of the assets. An arrangement in contravention is voidable at the instance of the company, subject to the restitution and bona fide third-party protections in the section.
content.glance: Non-cash acquisition of assets between company and director/connected person (or holding/subsidiary/associate directors) needs prior GM resolution (and holding-company GM if relevant); notice states value; breach is voidable subject to statutory protections.
content.study: A company shall not enter into an arrangement by which (a) a director of the company or its holding, subsidiary or associate company or a person connected with him acquires or is to acquire assets for consideration other than cash, from the company; or (b) the company acquires or is to acquire assets for consideration other than cash, from such a director or person so connected, unless prior approval for such arrangement is accorded by a resolution of the company in general meeting. If the director or connected person is a director of its holding company, resolution of the holding company in general meeting is also required. Notice for approval of the resolution must include the particulars of the arrangement along with the value of the assets involved. Any arrangement entered into in contravention is voidable at the instance of the company unless restitution is no longer possible and the company has been indemnified, or any rights acquired bona fide for value and without notice of contravention by any other person would be affected. Current-law framing: identify non-cash asset arrangement with director or connected person; require prior GM resolution (and holding-company resolution if applicable); check notice content; apply voidability and protections.

sections.heading: Prohibition
sections.body: Company must not enter into a non-cash asset arrangement with a director of the company or of its holding, subsidiary or associate company, or a person connected with him, without prior GM approval.

sections.heading: Holding-Company Approval
sections.body: If the director or connected person is a director of the holding company, the holding company’s general meeting must also approve.

sections.heading: Notice
sections.body: Notice of the resolution must include particulars of the arrangement and the value of the assets.

sections.heading: Consequence
sections.body: Arrangement in contravention is voidable at the instance of the company, subject to restitution impossibility with indemnity, and bona fide third-party rights.

provisions.title: Restriction on non-cash transactions involving directors

examples.title: Director buys company land for shares
examples.body: A director is to acquire a substantial parcel of company land in exchange for shares rather than cash. Section 192 requires prior approval by a resolution of the company in general meeting, with notice stating the value.

examples.title: Holding-company director
examples.body: The arrangement is with a director of the holding company. Both the company’s and the holding company’s general meetings must approve under s. 192.

hypotheticals.question: Is Board approval alone enough for a non-cash asset deal with a director?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 192 requires prior approval by a resolution of the company in general meeting (and of the holding company where applicable). Board approval is not a substitute.

distinctions.title: Non-cash transactions with directors (s. 192) vs related-party transactions (s. 188)
distinctions.left: Non-cash asset acquisitions involving directors/connected persons; GM approval
distinctions.right: Broader list of RPT contract types; Board and sometimes member approval

misconceptions.trap: Only cash deals with directors need scrutiny; non-cash exchanges are free of member approval.
misconceptions.correction: Section 192 specifically targets non-cash asset arrangements with directors and connected persons and requires prior general-meeting approval.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 192 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify non-cash asset arrangement with director/connected person. II. Require prior GM resolution (and holding-company GM if needed). III. Check notice content. IV. Apply voidability. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Arrangement facts; approval status; notice; precise relief.

examTips: Non-cash asset deals with directors need prior GM approval.
Holding-company GM if director is of the holding company.
Voidable on breach, with statutory protections.
